title: Learn versioned jurisdiction and committee fingerprints
summary: Learn descriptive procedural and interaction regularities for a jurisdiction/body/meeting type while preserving source/profile versions, applicability, uncertain support and temporal regimes. These fingerprints guide experiments; they do not establish authority or verified identity.
in_scope: Inherited profile and jurisdiction override references
out_of_scope: Replacing reviewed crawler rules with learned regularities
Training on the held-out meeting or future role changes
implementation: Define fingerprint manifests with jurisdiction/body/meeting-type, source profile digest, cohort/provenance groups, cutoff, feature/extractor versions and supporting spans.
Aggregate anonymous procedural patterns across eligible meetings with group-balanced support, keeping per-feature coverage and variability instead of a single certainty score.
Compare a generic meeting profile, a sourced local-rule profile, and an empirically learned profile on the same frozen cohort; preserve unknown profiles as a valid condition.
Detect chair/rule/meeting-mode regime changes; propose a new profile version with effective and availability times instead of rewriting historical profile behavior.
Export descriptive profile references and qualified applicability only, leaving legal capability and person assignment to their separate owners.

acceptance.criterion: A fingerprint cannot contain test-meeting/future evidence or silently cross body/jurisdiction scope.
acceptance.verification: Run train/test/source-group contamination sentinels and validate rejected profile manifests.

acceptance.criterion: Changing the chair or meeting type creates a separately applicable regime instead of retroactively changing old assessments.
acceptance.verification: Replay profile versions over chronological meetings with an explicit transition source.

acceptance.criterion: Learned regularities and reviewed procedural rules remain distinct in packets and reports.
acceptance.verification: Inspect profile fields, provider-visible state and assessment explanations in a paired comparison.

acceptance.criterion: A no-profile or unsupported-profile case is reported and remains evaluable.
acceptance.verification: Run missing/ambiguous institution controls without dropping their query segments.

tests: Different meeting type with shared participants
Profile trained on a re-encoded copy of held-out hearing
risks: Institutional scripts may dominate individual behavior signals.
Small repeated-participant corpora can overfit meeting production practices.

reuse.application: Reuse group-balanced descriptive aggregation concepts without converting them into identity probability.
Keep local sourced conventions as a separate baseline/profile reference.

sources: User clarification, 2026-10-08, active Matter build: DIAT owns meeting learning; roughly 315 hours/5–10 recurring people is user-reported; crawler owns jurisdiction knowledge; private exported-data experiments only.
Original repository inputs: matterbrainstormspec; matterjevmesh; jevinmatter (brainstorming, not implementation evidence).
